rationale: The first reply correctly pointed to moisture and badly seated caps, advised isolating and drying, and asked a useful question, though it repeated the cap-seating point twice. The second reply bolted on a generic water-near-electrics warning that ignores the customer's evidence (the hob was unplugged, dried, and is now fine) and tells them not to use the hob until an electrician checks it. That contradicts its own next line, 'Good news, that has sorted it', so the escalation is unneeded and the message is incoherent. It also omitted the sensible advice to call an engineer if the clicking returns after drying, and never confirmed there was no gas smell.
